paragraphs.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֵ֛ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה לֵאמֹֽר׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And the Elohim spoke all these words, saying:

notes.official: **The Decalogue-speech introduction.** The Hebrew text uses *ʾĕlōhîm* (not YHWH) as the speech-introduction subject — a Priestly-source feature. The threefold enumeration-traditions (Jewish-Masoretic; Augustinian/Catholic/Lutheran; Orthodox/Reformed) are documented at the central entry `aseret-ha-dvarim-decalogue-enumeration-jewish-vs-augustinian-orthodox-cross-corpus`. The WoH-Translation preserves the Jewish-Masoretic enumeration per the source-text.

paragraphs.text: אָֽנֹכִ֖י֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֧ר הוֹצֵאתִ֛יךָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם מִבֵּ֣֥ית עֲבָדִֽ֑ים׃

i18n.en: "I am YHWH your Elohim, who brought you out from the land of Mitsrayim, from the house of slaves.

notes.official: **The First Word (Jewish enumeration) / Prologue (Augustinian-Reformed enumeration).** *ʾānōḵî YHWH ʾĕlōhêḵā ʾăšer hôṣēʾṯîḵā mē-ʾereṣ miṣrayim mibbêṯ ʿăḇāḏîm* 'I am YHWH your Elohim, who brought you out from the land of Mitsrayim, from the house of slaves'. See the central entries for the multi-tradition enumeration documentation (no adjudication) and the *ʾānōḵî YHWH* divine self-identification formula's cross-corpus reach to the Holiness Code, Deutero-Isaiah, Ezek 20.

paragraphs.text: לֹֽ֣א יִהְיֶֽה־לְךָ֛֩ אֱלֹהִ֥֨ים אֲחֵרִ֖֜ים עַל־פָּנָֽ֗יַ

i18n.en: You shall have no other elohim before my face.

notes.official: **The no-other-elohim prohibition.** *lōʾ yihĕyeh lĕḵā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm ʿal-pānāy* 'you shall have no other elohim before my face'. The literal *ʾĕlōhîm* plural-translation and the literal *ʿal-pānāy* 'before my face' are preserved; the monolatry-vs-monotheism scholarly dispute (Smith 2002, Albertz 1994) is documented at the central entry without adjudication.

i18n.en: You shall not make for yourself a carved image, nor any likeness of what is in the heavens above, or what is in the earth beneath, or what is in the waters beneath the earth.

notes.official: **The image-prohibition.** The doubled *pesel + tĕmûnâ* construct is preserved. See the central entry `pesel-utemunah-graven-image-iconographic-prohibition-cross-corpus` for the Mettinger 1995 *No Graven Image?* framework, the cross-corpus reach to Deut 4:15-19 and the Golden-Calf incident (Ex 32), and the prophetic anti-idolatry polemic tradition.

paragraphs.text: לֹֽא־תִשְׁתַּחְוֶ֥֣ה לָהֶ֖ם֮ וְלֹ֣א תָעָבְדֵ֑ם֒ כִּ֣י אָֽנֹכִ֞י יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ אֵ֣ל קַנָּ֔א פֹּ֠קֵד עֲוֺ֨ן אָבֹ֧ת עַל־בָּנִ֛ים עַל־שִׁלֵּשִׁ֥ים וְעַל־רִבֵּעִ֖ים לְשֹׂנְאָֽ֑י׃

i18n.en: You shall not bow down to them, and you shall not serve them; for I, YHWH your Elohim, am a jealous El, visiting the iniquity of fathers upon sons, upon the third and the fourth generation of those who hate me,

notes.official: *ʾēl qannāʾ* 'a jealous El' — the El-as-divine-name preservation. The *poqed ʿawon* 'visiting iniquity' formula across three-and-four generations; cross-corpus to Ex 34:7, Num 14:18, Deut 5:9; the prophetic-reversal at Ezek 18, Jer 31:29-30.

paragraphs.text: וְעֹ֥֤שֶׂה חֶ֖֙סֶד֙ לַאֲלָפִ֑֔ים לְאֹהֲבַ֖י וּלְשֹׁמְרֵ֥י מִצְוֺתָֽי׃ (ס)

i18n.en: and showing chesed to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments.

paragraphs.text: לֹ֥א תִשָּׂ֛א אֶת־שֵֽׁם־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ לַשָּׁ֑וְא כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יְנַקֶּה֙ יְהוָ֔ה אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־יִשָּׂ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ לַשָּֽׁוְא׃ (פ)

i18n.en: You shall not lift up the name of YHWH your Elohim in vain, for YHWH will not hold guiltless the one who lifts up his name in vain.

notes.official: **The name-of-YHWH-in-vain prohibition.** *lōʾ ṯiśśāʾ ʾeṯ-šēm-YHWH ʾĕlōhêḵā la-ššāwʾ* 'you shall not lift up the name of YHWH your Elohim in vain'. The literal *lōʾ ṯiśśāʾ* 'you shall not lift up' is preserved rather than the colloquial 'you shall not take'. See the central entry for the perjury-reading vs profane-utterance reading dispute and the post-biblical Tetragrammaton-substitution tradition.

paragraphs.text: זָכ֛וֹר֩ אֶת־י֥֨וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֖֜ת לְקַדְּשֽׁ֗וֹ

i18n.en: Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.

notes.official: **The Sabbath commandment with creation-grounding (Ex 20:8-11).** The Deut 5:12-15 parallel grounds the Sabbath in the Exodus-deliverance instead. The rabbinic *zakhor-shamor* reconciliation 'remember and observe were said in a single utterance' (b. Rosh Hashanah 27a) harmonizes the two versions. See the central entry for the dual-grounding theological-significance.

paragraphs.text: שֵׁ֤֣שֶׁת יָמִ֣ים֙ תַּֽעֲבֹ֔ד֮ וְעָשִׂ֖֣יתָ כָּל־מְלַאכְתֶּֽךָ֒

i18n.en: Six days you shall labor and do all your work,

paragraphs.text: וְי֙וֹם֙ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔֜י שַׁבָּ֖֣ת ׀ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑֗יךָ לֹֽ֣א־תַעֲשֶׂ֣֨ה כָל־מְלָאכָ֡֜ה אַתָּ֣ה ׀ וּבִנְךָֽ֣־וּ֠בִתֶּ֗ךָ עַבְדְּךָ֤֨ וַאֲמָֽתְךָ֜֙ וּבְהֶמְתֶּ֔֗ךָ וְגֵרְךָ֖֙ אֲשֶׁ֥֣ר בִּשְׁעָרֶֽ֔יךָ

i18n.en: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to YHWH your Elohim; you shall not do any work — you, nor your son, nor your daughter, nor your manservant, nor your maidservant, nor your animal, nor the sojourner who is within your gates.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י שֵֽׁשֶׁת־יָמִים֩ עָשָׂ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם וְאֶת־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֶת־הַיָּם֙ וְאֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֔ם וַיָּ֖נַח בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֑י עַל־כֵּ֗ן בֵּרַ֧ךְ יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־י֥וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֖ת וַֽיְקַדְּשֵֽׁהוּ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: For in six days YHWH made the heavens and the earth, the sea, and all that is in them, and rested on the seventh day; therefore YHWH blessed the Sabbath day and made it holy.

notes.official: The Sabbath-rest grounded in the six-days-of-creation pattern (Gen 2:1-3). The cosmological-anthropological universal significance contrasts with the Deut 5:15 social-historical liberation-significance.

paragraphs.text: כַּבֵּ֥ד אֶת־אָבִ֖יךָ וְאֶת־אִמֶּ֑ךָ לְמַ֙עַן֙ יַאֲרִכ֣וּן יָמֶ֔יךָ עַ֚ל הָאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לָֽךְ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be long upon the land which YHWH your Elohim gives you.

notes.official: Honor-parents (Fifth Word in Jewish, Augustinian, and Orthodox/Reformed enumerations alike). The *kabbed* (Piʿel) 'honor / treat-as-weighty' verb; the long-life land-promise *lĕ-maʿan yaʾăriḵûn yāmêḵā* establishes the consequence-of-obedience pattern that recurs throughout the Deuteronomic tradition.

i18n.en: You shall not murder. You shall not commit adultery. You shall not steal. You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.

notes.official: **The murder/adultery/theft/false-witness prohibitions.** In MT verse-numbering all four are one verse (20:13); the English-translation tradition splits them (20:13/14/15/16). The WoH-Translation preserves MT-numbering per the source-text Masoretic convention. The *rṣḥ* 'to murder' decision (overlay entry `ratsach-murder-vs-kill-decalogue-translation-convention-exodus-overlay`) preserves the modern critical *rṣḥ*-as-unlawful-killing-specifically reading.

paragraphs.text: לֹ֥א תַחְמֹ֖ד בֵּ֣ית רֵעֶ֑ךָ לֹֽא־תַחְמֹ֞ד אֵ֣שֶׁת רֵעֶ֗ךָ וְעַבְדּ֤וֹ וַאֲמָתוֹ֙ וְשׁוֹר֣וֹ וַחֲמֹר֔וֹ וְכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְרֵעֶֽךָ׃ (פ)

i18n.en: You shall not covet your neighbor's house; you shall not covet your neighbor's wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that belongs to your neighbor."

notes.official: **The Tenth Word (Jewish enumeration) / Ninth-and-Tenth (Augustinian enumeration) / Tenth (Orthodox-Reformed enumeration).** The *chamad* 'to covet' verb with the contested psychological-state vs action-oriented semantic range; see the overlay entry.

paragraphs.text: וְכָל־הָעָם֩ רֹאִ֨ים אֶת־הַקּוֹלֹ֜ת וְאֶת־הַלַּפִּידִ֗ם וְאֵת֙ ק֣וֹל הַשֹּׁפָ֔ר וְאֶת־הָהָ֖ר עָשֵׁ֑ן וַיַּ֤רְא הָעָם֙ וַיָּנֻ֔עוּ וַיַּֽעַמְד֖וּ מֵֽרָחֹֽק׃

i18n.en: And all the people were seeing the thunders and the torches, and the sound of the shofar, and the mountain smoking; and the people saw and trembled, and they stood at a distance.

notes.official: **The synaesthesia**: *wĕ-ḵol-hā-ʿām rōʾîm ʾeṯ-ha-qōlōṯ* 'and all the people were seeing the thunders'. The 'seeing the thunders' synaesthesia is a deliberate rhetorical-theological move (the people experience the theophany as a multi-sensory event in which the visual and auditory registers cross). The lapidim 'torches/lightnings' deploys the storm-theophany imagery.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה דַּבֵּר־אַתָּ֥ה עִמָּ֖נוּ וְנִשְׁמָ֑עָה וְאַל־יְדַבֵּ֥ר עִמָּ֛נוּ אֱלֹהִ֖ים פֶּן־נָמֽוּת׃

i18n.en: And they said to Moses, "You speak with us, and we will listen; but let the Elohim not speak with us, lest we die."

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֣ה אֶל־הָעָם֮ אַל־תִּירָאוּ֒ כִּ֗י לְבַֽעֲבוּר֙ נַסּ֣וֹת אֶתְכֶ֔ם בָּ֖א הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וּבַעֲב֗וּר תִּהְיֶ֧ה יִרְאָת֛וֹ עַל־פְּנֵיכֶ֖ם לְבִלְתִּ֥י תֶחֱטָֽאוּ׃

i18n.en: And Moses said to the people, "Do not fear, for it is in order to test you that the Elohim has come, and in order that the fear of him may be on your faces, that you may not sin."

paragraphs.text: וַיַּעֲמֹ֥ד הָעָ֖ם מֵרָחֹ֑ק וּמֹשֶׁה֙ נִגַּ֣שׁ אֶל־הָֽעֲרָפֶ֔ל אֲשֶׁר־שָׁ֖ם הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And the people stood at a distance, but Moses drew near to the thick darkness where the Elohim was.

notes.official: **The *ʿărāp̄el* 'thick darkness / dense cloud' divine-presence indicator**: Moses approaches the *ʿărāp̄el* where the Elohim is. Cross-corpus to 1 Kgs 8:12 (Solomon's temple-dedication theophany), Ps 18:9 ('thick darkness was under his feet'), Ps 97:2 ('clouds and thick darkness are round about him'), Joel 2:2, Zeph 1:15. The Moses-as-mediator institutional grounding for the prophetic office is established.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה כֹּ֥ה תֹאמַ֖ר אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אַתֶּ֣ם רְאִיתֶ֔ם כִּ֚י מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי עִמָּכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And YHWH said to Moses, "Thus you shall say to the children of Yisra'el: 'You yourselves have seen that I have spoken with you from the heavens.

notes.official: *min-ha-šāmayim dibbartî ʿimmāḵem* 'I have spoken with you from the heavens'. The from-the-heavens designation locates the divine speech in the cosmological-heavens register; cross-corpus to Deut 4:36.

paragraphs.text: לֹ֥א תַעֲשׂ֖וּן אִתִּ֑י אֱלֹ֤הֵי כֶ֙סֶף֙ וֵאלֹהֵ֣י זָהָ֔ב לֹ֥א תַעֲשׂ֖וּ לָכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: You shall not make alongside me elohim of silver, and elohim of gold you shall not make for yourselves.

notes.official: *ʾĕlōhê ḵesep̄ wē-ʾlōhê zāhāḇ* 'elohim of silver and elohim of gold' — preserves the elohim-plural for foreign-gods. Cross-corpus to the Golden-Calf incident (Ex 32) and the broader anti-idolatry polemic.

paragraphs.text: מִזְבַּ֣ח אֲדָמָה֮ תַּעֲשֶׂה־לִּי֒ וְזָבַחְתָּ֣ עָלָ֗יו אֶת־עֹלֹתֶ֙יךָ֙ וְאֶת־שְׁלָמֶ֔יךָ אֶת־צֹֽאנְךָ֖ וְאֶת־בְּקָרֶ֑ךָ בְּכָל־הַמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַזְכִּ֣יר אֶת־שְׁמִ֔י אָב֥וֹא אֵלֶ֖יךָ וּבֵרַכְתִּֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: An altar of earth you shall make for me, and you shall sacrifice on it your burnt-offerings and your peace-offerings, your sheep and your cattle. In every place where I cause my name to be remembered, I will come to you and bless you.

notes.official: **The altar law**: *mizbaḥ ʾăḏāmâ* 'an altar of earth' — the simple-earth-altar regulation. Cross-corpus to Deut 27:5-6, Josh 8:30-31 (Joshua's Mt-Ebal altar) — the cross-corpus deployment of the altar-law in the Joshua-land-entry narrative.

paragraphs.text: וְאִם־מִזְבַּ֤ח אֲבָנִים֙ תַּֽעֲשֶׂה־לִּ֔י לֹֽא־תִבְנֶ֥ה אֶתְהֶ֖ן גָּזִ֑ית כִּ֧י חַרְבְּךָ֛ הֵנַ֥פְתָּ עָלֶ֖יהָ וַתְּחַֽלְלֶֽהָ׃

i18n.en: And if you make for me an altar of stones, you shall not build them of hewn stone; for if you have wielded your sword upon it, you have profaned it.

notes.official: **The no-hewn-stone altar law**: *lōʾ-ṯiḇneh ʾeṯhen gāzîṯ* 'you shall not build them of hewn stone'. The profanation-by-iron-tool rationale; cross-corpus to 1 Macc 4:47 (Maccabean rebuilding of the altar per these terms).

paragraphs.text: וְלֹֽא־תַעֲלֶ֥ה בְמַעֲלֹ֖ת עַֽל־מִזְבְּחִ֑י אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־תִגָּלֶ֥ה עֶרְוָתְךָ֖ עָלָֽיו׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And you shall not go up by steps to my altar, that your nakedness may not be exposed upon it."

notes.official: **The no-steps-on-altar law**: the nakedness-exposure rationale. The Hebrew Bible's cultic-modesty regulation; cross-corpus to Ex 28:42-43 (the priestly-undergarments regulation for the same nakedness-on-altar concern).
